name: Brad Idzik

views.text: Deep passing is a timing problem; fix the routes and the quarterback's deep ball follows.
Receivers develop through detail and repetition, not through one big day.
A quarterback who slides and protects himself is making a smart football play, not a soft one.
A win built on protecting the ball and getting it out on time counts even when the yardage is low.
The head coach calls the plays; the coordinator's job is to have the plan and the players ready.
A young quarterback and young receivers grow together; their connection is a season-long project.

signatures: opens a press conference with a light personal story before turning to the football
thanks staff and players by name, down to small favors
explains a quarterback's good day through specific mechanics like timing and ball security

motivation.want: to grow from a trusted position coach into a respected coordinator
motivation.fear: being seen only as the head coach's friend

voice: Friendly, lighthearted and a little playful at the podium, he likes a personal anecdote before business. On football he is detail-first and encouraging, crediting the quarterback's growth and the receivers' work. Coverage is thin, so his voice is drawn mostly from team-site pieces.

evidence.summary: Report that Idzik, 32, will be Carolina's OC without calling plays (Canales will). He has never called plays, is known for developing receivers, spent four seasons with Canales in Seattle and followed him to Tampa Bay, and played receiver at Wake Forest. Background only.

Staff announcement naming Idzik, who coached under Canales in Seattle and Tampa Bay, as offensive coordinator alongside the retained Evero; Canales stresses continuity. Shows the working relationship, not its private nature.
Reports Carolina asked to interview the Bucs receivers coach; notes four years with Canales on Carroll's Seattle staff and that he followed Canales to Tampa. No quotes about his personality.

Notebook: he opens his Halloween presser thanking staff by name for candy and telling stories of homemade childhood costumes, then talks about receivers' route timing on deep balls and Bryce Young's improving connection with young wideouts. Team-site, light in tone.

evidence.publisher: Carolina Panthers (panthers.com), Darin Gantt and Kassidy Hill
evidence.summary: Idzik says he is comfortable with Young sliding to avoid late hits and credits him for protecting the ball and throwing on time in a shutout win with modest passing yards. Short quotes on one week.
